Regarding DW Fixer, I have an idea for why he appears younger.

I think that while he and the operative were fighting each other (See Charge and Undivided Attention), their blood mixed. We know that the fight was bloody (given the stabbing, bloody knuckles, and card artwork).  The massive scar doesn't appear to be from Undivided attention (in that it depicts the sword going through his shoulder), but it certainly seems plausible that it could be a result of that specific fight.  

Now, if their blood mixed, he might have gotten a dose of the chemical cocktail that keeps the Operative young, and gives her strength and enhanced recuperative abilities.  

This could explain why DW Fixer looks younger (or at least less grey) and beefier, in that the shared blood has given him a measure of his youth back.

This might explain the signifigance of the Dragon tattoo over the scar- it is the same design as the Operative has coiled around her arm.

If you want to get metaphysical, it could also explain the "bitter" portion of Bitter Strike, in that he's only alive because of his greatest enemy (and one that he might have prevented if he hadn't given up teaching when she needed it most...)

Edit: After a quick search of terms and some cross references, information about Dragon mythology is pretty sparse outside of RPG stats lmao. However, there were some interesting things I noted. Some of the more powerful Dragons in early Chinese mythology (namely the Dragon Kings) could shapeshift into human form. There is also a dragon called ZhuYin with a serpents body and the head of a human (pictures of that are hillarious). 

Trying to directly find a Chinese Dragon of Life/Death (I really tried to shoe horn it man) proved fruitless. But, I did turn up something of note. That dragon I mentioned with a serpents body and human head? Get this. The opening and closing of his eye represented the rising and setting sun. Now, call me crazy, but I swear I just made a huge topic about Ra-Horus that linked the rising and setting sun as a metaphore for Ra's death and rebirth. And, even more interestingly, that Dragon's influence is also said to reach down into the underworld. 

You are all free to draw your own conclusions there.
